done_when: In the machine's agent line, a waiting run for an item that other planned work waits on starts before runs nothing waits on, first-come within each group, and its place in line says why. New and existing client repos get it on init or upgrade plus sync, and a test covers both.

findings.body: Raise: Not done — The Machine tab shows `waiting #<place>` without saying why that run has its place. The changed `forge lanes` text prints a reason, but `src/forge/mod/hooks/machine.ts:64` and `:203` still render the waiting position and session line without using the new `unblocks` field. An agent watching the Machine tab cannot tell why a prerequisite moved ahead. The new test checks command output and JSON positions, but not the displayed explanation.
findings.title: Not done: In the machine's agent line, a waiting run for an item that other planned work waits on starts before runs nothing waits on, first

findings.body: Raise: Scale — `_unblocks` checks every story state on the landed branch, including completed stories, by launching a separate `git show` for each key before the run joins the queue. A long-lived client repo with 500 completed stories therefore incurs at least 500 Git subprocess reads on every work or review admission, even when no planned work remains. This delay grows without bound as stories accumulate.
findings.title: Scanning every historical story delays each agent admission

stop.reason: Owner chose narrow: check only stories still in progress so admission stays fast; the pane's why line is left for later, the forge command still shows why

why: The machine's agent line is first-come, so a part other work waits on queues behind new fixes
